topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These opening remarks introduce the lecture on cancer evolution and outline the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic mechanisms of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cell-intrinsic genetic mutations and epigenetic alterations drive clonal selection and neoplastic transformation.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchy and cell of origin in tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the role of tissue stemness, differentiation hierarchies, and specific cells of origin in initiating and propagating tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental promotion and stromal dependence in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how inflammatory signals, environmental promoters, and supportive stroma enable cancer development and maintain established tumors.

topics.label: Experimental and computational methods for studying tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the sequencing, spatial profiling, and computational techniques used to investigate tumor evolution and cellular interactions.

topics.label: Multifactorial synthesis of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic integrates the interplay of mutational, epigenetic, cell-of-origin, and microenvironmental factors into a unified model of cancer development.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: These closing remarks conclude the session and preview the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
